comment: check_derating policy template: the built-in defaults, to edit for your own rules.
Save it in the project folder (next to the .PrjPcb) as derating_policy.json; check_derating reads it on every call and says so (policy.chosen_by project_file).
Leave out any key to keep its default. A policy argument on the tool call overrides this file for one call.

Ratios are the highest applied/rated voltage allowed (0.75 = 25% derating). Tables map imperial case codes (0201, 0402, 0603, ...) to numbers; a table here adds to or replaces the default entries it names.
name: Default derating policy
source: Altium's ceramic capacitor derating article and its schematic review checklist

_notes.ceramic_max_ratio: ceramics: at least 25% derating as standard (Altium's ceramic derating article)
_notes.ceramic_ripple_max_ratio: ceramics on a switching converter's input, output or switch node: at least 50% derating (same article)
_notes.tantalum_max_ratio: MnO2 tantalums: at least 20% headroom (Altium's schematic review checklist); 0.5 is common practice on low-impedance rails
_notes.tantalum_polymer_max_ratio: polymer tantalums: 0.8 (some makers allow 0.9 above 10 V rated)
_notes.electrolytic_max_ratio: aluminium electrolytic and polymer capacitors, and polarized ones of no stated kind
_notes.dc_bias_min_ratio: a Class II ceramic at this share of its rating or more gets a DC-bias loss band
_notes.dc_bias_max_case: the largest case the DC-bias check looks at
_notes.dc_bias_min_uf: per case, the capacitance in uF from which a part counts as high-value for its size
_notes.resistor_max_voltage: typical maximum working voltage per size, used when a part states none
_notes.resistor_power_w: typical power rating per size, used when a part states none
_notes.resistor_power_derating: info when a resistor dissipates more than this share of its rating
_notes.signal_max_v: the highest level assumed for a logic output driving an LED resistor
